:::{#exr-deriv-log-density}
#### Derivative of a density through its logarithm

Let $\p(\vx \mid \param)$ be a density
that is positive and differentiable in a scalar parameter $\param$.
Write $\deriv{\param}\p(\vx \mid \param)$
in terms of $\deriv{\param}\log \p(\vx \mid \param)$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-deriv-log-density}

By the chain rule,
with outer function $\log u$ and inner function $u = \p(\vx \mid \param)$:

$$
\deriv{\param} \log \p(\vx \mid \param)
= \paren{\frac{d}{du} \log u}\bigg|_{u = \p(\vx \mid \param)} \deriv{\param}\p(\vx \mid \param).
$$

The inner derivative $\deriv{\param}\p(\vx \mid \param)$ is the quantity we want,
so only the outer derivative needs working out:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d}{du} \log u
&= \frac{1}{u}
&& \text{(derivative of the natural logarithm)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging the outer derivative back in:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\param} \log \p(\vx \mid \param)
&= \frac{1}{\p(\vx \mid \param)} \deriv{\param}\p(\vx \mid \param)
&& \text{(outer derivative is $1/u$)}\\
\deriv{\param}\p(\vx \mid \param)
&= \paren{\deriv{\param} \log \p(\vx \mid \param)} \p(\vx \mid \param)
&& \text{(multiply both sides by $\p(\vx \mid \param) > 0$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
